questions.question: 58 + 79 - (31 + 25) times 2 + 61 - 17 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the expression using the BODMAS rule: Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

Bracket: (31 + 25) = 56

Multiplication: 56 × 2 = 112

Group addition: 58 + 79 + 61 = 198

Group subtraction: −112 − 17 = −129

Result: 198 − 129 = 69

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: 58 + 79 − (31 + 25) × 2 + 61 − 17

Method: BODMAS Rule (Brackets first, then Multiplication, then Addition/Subtraction)

⇒ 58 + 79 − (56) × 2 + 61 − 17

⇒ 58 + 79 − 112 + 61 − 17

⇒ (58 + 79 + 61) − 112 − 17

⇒ 198 − 112 − 17

⇒ 86 − 17

⇒ 69

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: Brackets (), Of/Orders, Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Types of Brackets

Standard order of solving brackets is Parenthesis (), then Braces {}, and finally Square Brackets [].

Calculation Shortcuts

Combine all positive numbers and all negative numbers separately before the final subtraction to reduce errors.

questions.question: 69 + (26 times 2) - 44 + 31 - 18 + 42 div 2 = ?

Apply BODMAS: solve multiplication inside brackets and division first.

⇒ 69 + 52 − 44 + 31 − 18 + 21

Combine positive and negative terms: (69 + 52 + 31 + 21) − (44 + 18)

⇒ 173 − 62 = 111

**∴ The correct answer is 111.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: 69 + (26 × 2) − 44 + 31 − 18 + 42 ÷ 2

Formula: BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 69 + 52 − 44 + 31 − 18 + 42 ÷ 2

⇒ 69 + 52 − 44 + 31 − 18 + 21

⇒ 121 − 44 + 31 − 18 + 21

⇒ 77 + 31 − 18 + 21

⇒ 108 − 18 + 21

⇒ 90 + 21

⇒ 111

**∴ The correct answer is 111.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the precedence of operations: Brackets (), Orders (xy, √), Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Left-to-Right Rule

When operations of the same priority (like ÷ and × or + and −) appear together, solve them in the order they occur from left to right.

Simplification Tip

To minimize calculation errors, group all positive terms and negative terms separately before performing the final subtraction.

questions.question: The ratio of the number of students in Class A to Class B is 4 : 5. If 8 students are transferred from B to A, the ratio becomes 5:6. Find the original number of students in each class.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total students remain constant: Sum of initial ratio (4+5=9) and final ratio (5+6=11).

Equalize sum: Initial (44 : 55) and Final (45 : 54) by multiplying 9 with 11 and 11 with 9.

Increase in Class A = 45 − 44 = 1 unit → 8 students.

Class A = 44 × 8 = 352 | Class B = 55 × 8 = 440.

**∴ The correct answer is A- 352, B- 440.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Ratio A : B = 4 : 5

Let the students in A be 4x and B be 5x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f016d0dd059baa68c93802e25aea31b1f7379c0a54512d24f1b5528b765413db.png] 

New ratio after transfer: (4x + 8) / (5x − 8) = 5 / 6

⇒ 6 × (4x + 8) = 5 × (5x − 8)

⇒ 24x + 48 = 25x − 40

⇒ 25x − 24x = 48 + 40

⇒ x = 88

⇒ Number of students in Class A = 4 × 88 = 352

⇒ Number of students in Class B = 5 × 88 = 440

**∴ The correct answer is A- 352, B- 440.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(a × b).

Duplicate and Sub-duplicate Ratio

Duplicate ratio of a : b is a² : b², while sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

Componendo and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b)/(a − b) = (c + d)/(c − d).

questions.question: Which of the following is greater than 0.overline{51} ?

Expand values to compare: Given = 0.5151...

Options: (1) 0.4747..., (2) 0.5000..., (3) 0.4949..., (4) 0.5333...

Comparing hundredths digits: Given (1) vs Option 4 (3).

Since 3 > 1, the value 0.5333... is greater than 0.5151...

**∴ The correct answer is 0.533...**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Target value X = 0.515151...

Formula: A recurring decimal 0.ab... can be compared by expanding it to several decimal places.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dea6bcfd00be778bfeb296d7619680ef85a037adb6e103175dfadac8f9a404c.png] 

⇒ Option 1: 0.4747... (Hundredth digit 7 is less than tenth digit 5 of target)

⇒ Option 2: 0.4999... = 0.5 (Hundredth digit 0 is less than hundredth digit 1 of target)

⇒ Option 3: 0.4949... (Tenth digit 4 is less than tenth digit 5 of target)

⇒ Option 4: 0.5333... (Hundredth digit 3 is greater than hundredth digit 1 of target)

⇒ 0.5333... > 0.5151...

**∴ The correct answer is 0.533...**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pure Recurring Decimals

A decimal where all digits after the decimal point repeat. Formula: 0.xyxy... = xy ÷ 99.

Mixed Recurring Decimals

A decimal where some digits do not repeat. Formula: 0.abc... = (abc − ab) ÷ 900 where c repeats.

The 0.999... Property

A recurring decimal ending in 9 can be simplified. For example, 0.4999... is exactly equal to 0.5.

questions.question: 750(1)/(3) + 750(1)/(15) + 750(1)/(35) + dots + 750(1)/(99) = ?

questions.question: If sqrt{506.25} = 22.5 , then what is the value of sqrt{0.00050625} ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Decimal Rule: Shifting the decimal point **2n places** inside a square root shifts it **n places** in the final result.

Compare **506.25** and **0.00050625**: The decimal moves **6 places** to the left.

Therefore, in the answer **22.5**, move the decimal 6 ÷ 2 = **3 places** to the left.

22.5 → 2.25 → 0.225 → **0.0225**.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.0225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** √506.25 = 22.5

**Formula Used:** √(a ÷ b) = √a ÷ √b

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82e161b441db8ab403b886d5d3a5ca632ba32cb9786f95dd1ed24ef99e6385b5.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ √0.00050625 = √(506.25 ÷ 1,000,000)

⇒ √0.00050625 = √506.25 ÷ √1,000,000

⇒ √0.00050625 = 22.5 ÷ 1,000

⇒ √0.00050625 = 0.0225

**∴ The correct answer is 0.0225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root Decimal Property

If a number has **2n** decimal places, its square root will have exactly **n** decimal places.

Perfect Square Ending in 25

A number ending in 25 always has a square root ending in 5. Example: √625 = 25, √2025 = 45.

Powers of 10

The square root of 10²ⁿ is always 10ⁿ. For example, √10000 = 100.

questions.question: The product of the three consecutive odd numbers is 1287. What is the sum of the largest and the smallest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Approximate the **cube root** of the product: √³1287 ≈ 10.87.

The **consecutive odd numbers** near 10.87 are 9, 11, and 13.

Check: 9 × 11 × 13 = 1287 (Matches given product).

Sum of **largest** (13) and **smallest** (9) = 9 + 13 = 22.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Product of **three consecutive odd numbers** = 1287.

**Formula Used:** Product of terms = (x − 2) × x × (x + 2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f1c4cc9c8ea2b0796c3907337c68a82e89378a71506d5c42f7ca3c336172c06.png] 

⇒ Let the numbers be (x − 2), x, and (x + 2).

⇒ (x − 2) × x × (x + 2) = 1287

⇒ x(x² − 4) = 1287

⇒ Factorizing 1287: 1287 = 3 × 3 × 11 × 13 = 9 × 11 × 13

⇒ By comparison, x = 11.

⇒ Smallest number = 11 − 2 = 9

⇒ Largest number = 11 + 2 = 13

⇒ Sum = 9 + 13 = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Odd/Even Numbers

The difference between any two **consecutive odd** or **consecutive even** numbers is always 2.

Cube Root Estimation

For the product of three consecutive integers (n−1), n, (n+1), the product is approximately n³. This helps in quickly identifying the **middle term**.

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

Consecutive odd numbers form an **Arithmetic Progression** with common difference d = 2. The sum of n terms is Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n−1)d].

questions.question: If a = 3 + sqrt{2}, b = 3 - sqrt{2} , then what is the value of a² + b² ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For conjugates a = x + √y and b = x − √y, the sum of squares is given by 2(x² + y).

Here x = 3 and √y = √2 ⇒ y = 2.

Calculation: 2 × (3² + 2) = 2 × (9 + 2) = 2 × 11 = 22.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: a = 3 + √2 and b = 3 − √2

Formula: (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy and (x − y)² = x² + y² − 2xy

⇒ a² = (3 + √2)² = 3² + (√2)² + 2 × 3 × √2 ⇒ a² = 9 + 2 + 6√2 = 11 + 6√2 ⇒ b² = (3 − √2)² = 3² + (√2)² − 2 × 3 × √2 ⇒ b² = 9 + 2 − 6√2 = 11 − 6√2 ⇒ a² + b² = (11 + 6√2) + (11 − 6√2) ⇒ a² + b² = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

For any two numbers, (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). This is useful for solving symmetric expressions.

Rationalization Conjugates

The product of conjugates (x + √y)(x − √y) = x² − y is always a rational number.

Algebraic Expansion

Square of a binomial: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.

questions.question: How many numbers among 1210, 1331, 1442, 1553 are divisible by 11?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisibility rule of 11: (Sum of digits at odd places) − (Sum of digits at even places) = 0 or a multiple of 11.

1210 → (1+1) − (2+0) = 0 (Divisible)

1331 → (1+3) − (3+1) = 0 (Divisible)

1442 → (1+4) − (4+2) = −1 (Not Divisible)

1553 → (1+5) − (5+3) = −2 (Not Divisible)

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given numbers: 1210, 1331, 1442, 1553

Method: Check each number by dividing it by 11 to see if the remainder is 0.

⇒ 1210 ÷ 11 = 110 (Remainder = 0)

⇒ 1331 ÷ 11 = 121 (Remainder = 0)

⇒ 1442 ÷ 11 = 131 with remainder 1

⇒ 1553 ÷ 11 = 141 with remainder 2

⇒ Total numbers divisible by 11 = 1210 and 1331

⇒ Count of divisible numbers = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by 11 (Detailed)

Subtract the last digit from the rest of the digits. If the result is divisible by 11, the original number is too (e.g., 121 → 12 − 1 = 11).

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by both 9 and 11?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

A number is divisible by 11 if the alternating sum of its digits is 0 or a multiple of 11.

For 7920: Sum = 7 + 9 + 2 + 0 = 18 (Divisible by 9).

Alternating difference: (7 + 2) − (9 + 0) = 9 − 9 = 0 (Divisible by 11).

**∴ The correct answer is 7920.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers (1) 7920, (2) 8250, (3) 8020, (4) 8163

**Formula Used:** Divisibility by 9 (Sum of digits) and Divisibility by 11 (Sum of odd place digits − Sum of even place digits).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ecee3399cfed9812fa8e883f5d5b9116f63d488ff4fae41da2d507bf6dd05d7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For 7920: Sum = 18 (divisible by 9). Diff = (7+2) − (9+0) = 0 (divisible by 11). Correct.

⇒ For 8250: Sum = 15 (not divisible by 9). Diff = (8+5) − (2+0) = 11 (divisible by 11). Incorrect.

⇒ For 8020: Sum = 10 (not divisible by 9). Diff = (8+2) − (0+0) = 10 (not divisible by 11). Incorrect.

⇒ For 8163: Sum = 18 (divisible by 9). Diff = (8+6) − (1+3) = 10 (not divisible by 11). Incorrect.

**∴ The correct answer is 7920.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 99

A number is divisible by 99 if and only if it is divisible by both 9 and 11. Alternatively, if you group digits in pairs from the right, their sum must be divisible by 99 (e.g., 79 + 20 = 99).

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3. This is a sub-condition for divisibility by 9.

Divisibility by 11 Property

The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and even places must be 0, 11, 22, or any multiple of 11 for the number to be divisible by 11.

questions.question: Average of first 'N' multiples of 3 is 66. What is the value of 'N'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average of first N multiples of a number k = k × (N + 1) ÷ 2

Given: k = 3 and Average = 66

3 × (N + 1) ÷ 2 = 66

(N + 1) ÷ 2 = 22

N + 1 = 44 ⇒ N = 43

**∴ The correct answer is 43.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First multiple of 3 = 3

Nth multiple of 3 = 3N

Average of multiples = 66

**Formula Used:**

Average of an Arithmetic Progression (AP) = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c95975eb20a27c3c1a58ed740cf6ce632ce731f23520378d695af082027421cd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average = (3 + 3N) ÷ 2

⇒ 66 = (3 + 3N) ÷ 2

⇒ 66 × 2 = 3 + 3N

⇒ 132 = 3 + 3N

⇒ 3N = 132 − 3

⇒ 3N = 129

⇒ N = 129 ÷ 3

⇒ N = 43

**∴ The correct answer is 43.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of first N natural numbers

The average of the first N natural numbers (1, 2, 3... N) is given by (N + 1) ÷ 2.

Sum of first N multiples

The sum of the first N multiples of a number k is k × N(N + 1) ÷ 2.

Average of consecutive numbers

For any sequence in Arithmetic Progression, the average is exactly the middle term (if N is odd) or the mean of the two middle terms (if N is even).

questions.question: Which Rashtrakuta chief overthrew his Chalukya overlord and founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dantidurga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dantidurga**, also known as **Dantivarman**, was the founder of the **Rashtrakuta Empire** in the **8th century**.
 
• He was initially a **feudatory** or a high-ranking official under the **Chalukyas of Badami**.
 
• In **753 AD**, he overthrew his **Chalukya overlord**, **Kirtivarman II**, and established the **Rashtrakuta dynasty** as a sovereign power.
 
• To legitimize his rule as a **Kshatriya** (since he was not born into that caste), he performed a ritual known as **Hiranya-garbha** (literally, the golden womb) at **Ujjain**.
 
• He assumed titles such as **Maharajadhiraja**, **Paramesvara**, and **Prithvivallabha**, signifying his supreme status over the Deccan region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Krishna I (reigned 756–774 AD):**

 
 
• He was the uncle of **Dantidurga** and succeeded him to the throne.
 
• He is most famous for the construction of the monolithic **Kailasa Temple** at **Ellora**, which is carved out of a single rock.
 
• He expanded the empire by completely ending the power of the **Chalukyas** and defeating the **Gangas of Mysore**.
 
 
 
• **Dhruva (reigned 780–793 AD):**
 
 
• One of the most powerful rulers who took the **Rashtrakuta** power to **North India**.
 
• He defeated the **Gurjara-Pratihara** king **Vatsaraja** and the **Pala** king **Dharmapala** during the **Tripartite Struggle** for the control of **Kannauj**.
 
• He was also known as **Dharavarsha**.
 
 
 
• **Amoghvarsha I (reigned 814–878 AD):**
 
 
• He was the longest-reigning **Rashtrakuta** king, ruling for **64 years**.
 
• Known as the **Ashoka of the South**, he was a patron of literature and art and a follower of **Jainism**.
 
• He authored **Kavirajamarga**, which is considered the first available work on poetics, rhetoric, and grammar in the **Kannada** language.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Rashtrakutas** ruled a vast territory comprising modern-day **Maharashtra**, **Karnataka**, and parts of **Andhra Pradesh** and **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• Their capital was established at **Manyakheta** (modern **Malkhed** near **Gulbarga**, **Karnataka**) during the reign of **Amoghvarsha I**.
 
• They were great patrons of rock-cut architecture, visible in the **Ellora** and **Elephanta Caves**.
 
• The dynasty was eventually overthrown in **973 AD** by **Tailapa II**, a feudatory who founded the **Western Chalukya Empire** (Chalukyas of Kalyani).

questions.question: The second five year plan of India was completed in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1961**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** of India was functional during the period from **1956 to 1961**. It officially concluded on **March 31, 1961**.
 
• This plan was based on the **P.C. Mahalanobis Model**, which prioritized **rapid industrialization** and the development of **heavy and basic industries**.
 
• The primary aim was to achieve a **socialistic pattern of society**, a goal adopted during the **Avadi Session** of the **Indian National Congress** in **1955**.
 
• It focused heavily on the **public sector** to drive the national economy, following the guidelines of the **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956**.
 
• The plan saw the establishment of major **hydroelectric power projects** and five **steel plants** at **Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela** with foreign collaboration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956):**

 
 
• It was based on the **Harrod-Domar Model** and focused mainly on **agriculture, price stability, and power**.
 
• It was a successful plan as it achieved a growth rate of **3.6%**, exceeding the target of **2.1%**.
 
 
 
• **Third Five-Year Plan (1961–1966):**
 
 
• This plan followed the completion of the second plan in **1961**. It aimed to make India a **self-reliant** and **self-generating economy**.
 
• However, due to the **Sino-Indian War (1962)** and the **Indo-Pakistani War (1965)**, the plan failed to meet its targets.
 
 
 
• **Plan Holidays (1966–1969):**
 
 
• Due to the failure of the Third Plan and the devaluation of the **Indian Rupee**, the government declared **Plan Holidays**.
 
• During this period, three **annual plans** were implemented instead of a comprehensive five-year strategy.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969–1974):**
 
 
• Launched under the leadership of **Indira Gandhi**, it focused on **growth with stability** and the 14 major **Indian banks were nationalized** in **1969**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Planning Commission** was the nodal agency responsible for drafting the Five-Year Plans. It was established on **March 15, 1950**.
 
• The **National Development Council (NDC)** was responsible for the final approval of these plans to ensure the participation of **State Governments**.
 
• In **January 2015**, the **NDA government** replaced the Planning Commission with the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India).
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** is often referred to as the **"Industrial and Transport Plan"** because nearly **28%** of the total outlay was dedicated to **transport and communications**, and **20%** to **industry and mining**.
 
• The targeted growth rate for the Second Plan was **4.5%**, but the actual growth achieved was approximately **4.27%**.

questions.question: As per the the Industrial Policy Statement, 1977 a tiny unit was one which has an investment of Rs. ____ lakh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Statement of 1977** was announced by the **Janata Party government** on **December 23, 1977**.
 
• This policy was presented in the **Parliament** by the then Union Minister of Industry, **George Fernandes**.
 
• The policy introduced the concept of the **"Tiny Sector"** for the first time to promote rural industrialization and decentralization.
 
• As per the 1977 policy, a **tiny unit** was defined as an industrial unit with an investment in **machinery and equipment** of up to **Rs. 1 lakh**.
 
• To qualify as a tiny unit, the enterprise also had to be located in **villages or towns** with a population of less than **50,000** according to the **1971 Census**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Focus of 1977 Policy**: The primary objective was the **effective promotion of cottage and small-scale industries** widely dispersed in rural areas and small towns. It aimed to generate **large-scale employment** and reduce the concentration of economic power.
 
• **Classification of Small Sector**: The policy divided the small sector into three distinct categories:
 
 
• **Cottage and Household Industries**: Aimed at providing self-employment.
 
• **Tiny Sector**: Investment up to **Rs. 1 lakh** in rural/semi-urban areas.
 
• **Small Scale Industries (SSI)**: Investment limit up to **Rs. 10 lakhs**.
 
 
 
• **District Industries Centers (DIC)**: The 1977 policy proposed the establishment of **DICs** in every district. These centers were designed to provide all the services and support required by small and tiny entrepreneurs, such as **raw materials, credit, and marketing assistance**, under a single roof.
 
• **Reservation of Items**: To protect small-scale industries from competition with large-scale industries, the number of items reserved for exclusive production in the small sector was increased from **180 to 504**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ancillary Units**: Under the same 1977 policy, the investment limit for **ancillary units** (units supplying parts to large industries) was set at **Rs. 15 lakhs**.
 
• **Revival of Khadi**: The policy placed a heavy emphasis on the **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** to promote the use of handloom fabrics and traditional crafts.
 
• **Policy Evolution**: The investment limits for the tiny sector were later revised in subsequent policies. In the **Industrial Policy Statement of 1980**, the limit for tiny units was increased to **Rs. 2 lakhs**.
 
• **Demographic Criteria**: The **50,000 population** threshold was a critical feature of the 1977 policy to ensure that industrial benefits reached the **rural hinterland** rather than being clustered around metropolitan hubs.

questions.question: Which of the following river is known as Dakshin Ganga?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Godavari** is the **largest peninsular river** system in India. Due to its **great age**, **large size**, and **vast expanse**, it is famously known as the **Dakshin Ganga** (Ganga of the South).
 
• It originates in the **Western Ghats** at **Trimbakeshwar** in the **Nashik** district of **Maharashtra**.
 
• The total length of the river is approximately **1,465 km**, making it the **second-longest river** in India after the **Ganga**.
 
• The **Godavari basin** extends over an area of about **3,12,812 sq. km**, which is nearly **9.5%** of the total geographical area of the country. It drains parts of **Maharashtra**, **Telangana**, **Andhra Pradesh**, **Chhattisgarh**, and **Odisha**.
 
• The river flows **eastward** across the **Deccan Plateau** and eventually discharges its water into the **Bay of Bengal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Narmada:**

 
 
• The **Narmada** is the **largest west-flowing river** of peninsular India.
 
• It rises from the **Amarkantak Plateau** in **Madhya Pradesh** at an elevation of about **1,057 meters**.
 
• It flows through a **rift valley** between the **Vindhya** and **Satpura** ranges and forms the famous **Dhuandhar Falls** near **Jabalpur**.
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra:**
 
 
• The **Brahmaputra** originates from the **Chemayungdung glacier** of the **Kailas range** near **Mansarovar lake** in **Tibet**.
 
• In **Tibet**, it is known as the **Tsangpo**. It enters India in **Arunachal Pradesh** as the **Siang** or **Dihang** river.
 
• It is known for having the **largest volume of water** among Indian rivers and is characterized by frequent **floods** and **channel shifting**.
 
 
 
• **Brahmani:**
 
 
• The **Brahmani** is a major seasonal river in the state of **Odisha**.
 
• It is formed by the confluence of the **Sankh** and **South Koel** rivers near **Rourkela**.
 
• It flows through the **Eastern Ghats** and joins the **Bay of Bengal** at **Dhamra**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tributaries of Godavari:** The main tributaries include the **Purna**, **Wardha**, **Pranhita**, **Manjra**, **Wainganga**, and **Penganga**. The **Pranhita** is the largest tributary, conveying the combined waters of the **Penganga**, **Wardha**, and **Wainganga**.
 
• **Religious Significance:** The river is considered sacred, and the **Kumbh Mela** is held at **Nashik** on its banks once every **12 years**.
 
• **Distinction between Dakshin Ganga and Ganga of the South:** While **Godavari** is officially referred to as **Dakshin Ganga**, the river **Kaveri** is sometimes called the "**Ganga of the South**" due to its ritual purity and spiritual importance in southern India.
 
• **Dams and Projects:** Several important projects are located on the Godavari, such as the **Jayakwadi Dam** in **Maharashtra** and the **Polavaram Project** in **Andhra Pradesh**, which provide significant irrigation and **hydroelectric power**.

questions.question: Lymph carries digested and absorbed fat from ______ and drains excess fluid from extra cellular space back into the blood.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**intestine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **lymphatic system** plays a crucial role in the human body by transporting **digested and absorbed fats** from the **intestine**. While most nutrients like glucose and amino acids are absorbed directly into the bloodstream, fats require a different pathway due to their size and chemical nature.
 
• Within the **villi** of the **small intestine**, there are specialized lymphatic capillaries known as **lacteals**. These lacteals are responsible for picking up dietary fats that have been processed into **chylomicrons** by the intestinal mucosal cells.
 
• Once absorbed, this fat-rich lymph, often called **chyle**, travels through the **lymphatic vessels** and eventually enters the systemic **blood circulation** through the **subclavian veins**.
 
• Another primary function of lymph is to maintain fluid balance. It drains **excess fluid** (interstitial fluid) from the **extracellular space** (the space between cells) and returns it to the **blood**. This prevents tissues from swelling and ensures that the total volume of blood remains stable.
 
• The lymph also acts as a transport medium for **lymphocytes** (white blood cells), which are essential for the body's **immune response** against pathogens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Small Intestine:** It is the primary site for **digestion** and **absorption** in the human body. It is divided into three parts: the **duodenum**, **jejunum**, and **ileum**. The presence of **villi** and **microvilli** significantly increases the **surface area** for nutrient uptake.
 
• **Lymph Composition:** Lymph is a **colorless fluid** similar in composition to **blood plasma** but with lower protein content. It contains high concentrations of **WBCs**, particularly **lymphocytes**, which help fight infections.
 
• **Other Organs (Options Analysis):**
 
 
• **Liver:** It produces **bile** for fat emulsification but does not serve as the primary site where lymph absorbs fat. It is located in the **upper right quadrant** of the abdomen.
 
• **Kidneys:** These are **excretory organs** responsible for filtering blood, removing **urea**, and maintaining **osmoregulation**. They are located on either side of the spine.
 
• **Pancreas:** It is a **glandular organ** that secretes **digestive enzymes** (like lipase and amylase) and hormones like **insulin**. It assists in digestion but does not absorb fats into the lymph.
 
 
 
• **Fat-Soluble Vitamins:** Along with fats, the **lacteals** in the **intestine** also facilitate the absorption of **fat-soluble vitamins**, which include **Vitamin A, D, E, and K**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Edema:** If the **lymphatic system** fails to drain excess fluid from the **extracellular space** efficiently, it leads to a condition called **edema**, characterized by swelling in tissues, often seen in the **legs and arms**.
 
• **Direction of Flow:** Unlike the circulatory system, which is a closed loop, the **lymphatic system** is a **one-way system**. Lymph flows only **towards the heart**, aided by the contraction of skeletal muscles and valves that prevent backflow.
 
• **Lymph Nodes:** These are small, bean-shaped structures located along the **lymphatic vessels** (e.g., in the **neck, armpits, and groin**) that act as filters to trap **bacteria, viruses,** and cancer cells.
 
• **Total Fluid Drainage:** On average, the lymphatic system returns about **2 to 3 liters** of fluid to the **bloodstream** every **24 hours**.

questions.question: The theory of Anekatavada is related to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Mahavira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anekantavada** is a core philosophical doctrine of **Jainism**, primarily propounded and systematized by **Lord Mahavira**, the **24th Tirthankara**.
 
• The term literally means **"non-absolutism"** or the **"theory of many-sidedness"**. It suggests that ultimate truth and reality are complex and have multiple aspects.
 
• According to this theory, no single point of view can provide a complete picture of the absolute truth. Only the **Kevalins** (omniscient beings) can comprehend reality in all its aspects, while ordinary humans perceive only a **partial truth**.
 
• It is closely related to the concepts of **Syadvada** (the theory of conditioned predication) and **Nayavada** (the theory of partial viewpoints), which provide the linguistic and logical framework for **Anekantavada**.
 
• This philosophy encourages **intellectual non-violence** and tolerance, as it acknowledges that different perspectives, even seemingly contradictory ones, can each contain an element of truth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Mahavira:**

 
 
• He was born in **540 BCE** (some sources say **599 BCE**) at **Kundagrama** near **Vaishali** in present-day **Bihar**.
 
• He belonged to the **Jnatrika clan** and was a contemporary of **Gautama Buddha**.
 
• At the age of **30**, he abandoned his royal life to become an ascetic and attained **Kevala Jnana** (enlightenment) at the age of **42**.
 
• He added the fifth vow of **Brahmacharya** (celibacy) to the four existing vows of **Parsvanatha** to form the **Pancha Mahavrata**.
 
 
 
• **Lord Buddha:**
 
 
• The founder of **Buddhism**, born as **Siddhartha Gautama** in **Lumbini**.
 
• His philosophy centers on the **Four Noble Truths** and the **Eightfold Path** (Astangika Marga). Unlike the Jain concept of an eternal soul (Jiva), Buddha preached **Anatta** (non-self) and **Anicca** (impermanence).
 
 
 
• **Vishnugupta:**
 
 
• Commonly known as **Chanakya** or **Kautilya**, he was the prime minister of **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• He is the author of the famous political treatise **Arthashastra**, which focuses on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
 
 
 
• **Samudragupta:**
 
 
• A prominent ruler of the **Gupta Dynasty**, often referred to as the **"Napoleon of India"** by historian **V.A. Smith** due to his extensive military conquests.
 
• His achievements are inscribed on the **Prayag Prashasti** (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), composed by his court poet **Harisena**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Syadvada:** This is the logical application of **Anekantavada**. It uses the particle **"Syat"** (meaning 'perhaps' or 'in a certain sense') to signify that every statement is relative to a particular point of view. There are **seven modes** of prediction in this system, known as **Saptabhanginaya**.
 
• **Core Tenets of Jainism:**
 
 
• **Ahimsa:** Extreme **non-violence** toward all living beings.
 
• **Triratna (Three Jewels):** These include **Samyak Darshana** (Right Faith), **Samyak Gyana** (Right Knowledge), and **Samyak Charitra** (Right Conduct).
 
• **Equality:** Jainism rejected the **Varna system** and emphasized that spiritual liberation is accessible to all, regardless of social status.
 
 
 
• **Jain Councils:**
 
 
• The **First Jain Council** was held at **Pataliputra** in the **3rd Century BCE**, presided over by **Sthulabhadra**.
 
• The **Second Jain Council** was held at **Vallabhi** in **512 CE**, where the final compilation of **12 Angas** and **12 Upangas** took place.

questions.question:
Which of the following is part of the Concurrent List of the Indian Constitution?

I. Public Health

II. Trade Unions
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the **Constitution of India** defines and specifies the allocation of powers and functions between the **Union** and the **States** through three distinct lists.
 
• **Statement I**: **Public Health** and sanitation, hospitals, and dispensaries are subjects categorized under the **State List (List II)** as per **Entry 6**. This implies that the **State Legislatures** have the primary jurisdiction to legislate on these matters. *Hence, statement I is incorrect.*
 
• **Statement II**: **Trade Unions**, along with industrial and labour disputes, are explicitly mentioned under the **Concurrent List (List III)** at **Entry 22**. This allows both the **Parliament of India** and the **State Legislatures** to create laws regarding them. *Hence, statement II is correct.*
 
• The **Concurrent List** is intended for subjects where a uniform national framework is beneficial, but individual states may also need to make specific provisions to suit their local conditions.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Only II**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Three Lists of the Seventh Schedule:**

 
 
• **Union List (List I)**: This list consists of subjects of **national importance** where only the **Parliament** has the exclusive power to legislate. It originally contained **97** subjects but currently has **100**. Notable examples include **Defense**, **Foreign Affairs**, **Railways**, **Banking**, and **Atomic Energy**.
 
• **State List (List II)**: This list consists of subjects of **regional or local importance**. It originally had **66** subjects but now contains **61**. Key subjects include **Police**, **Agriculture**, **Local Government**, **Public Order**, and **Land**.
 
• **Concurrent List (List III)**: This list comprises subjects where both the **Union** and **State Governments** can exercise power. It originally had **47** subjects and currently features **52**. Major subjects include **Education**, **Forests**, **Marriage and Divorce**, **Criminal Law**, and **Electricity**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Basis:**
 
 
• **Article 246** of the **Constitution of India** provides the legal basis for the distribution of legislative powers between the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• The concept of the **Concurrent List** in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the **Constitution of Australia**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976**: This significant amendment shifted five subjects from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**, namely **Education**, **Forests**, **Weights and Measures**, **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**, and **Administration of Justice**.
 
• **Conflict Resolution (Article 254)**: If there is a conflict between a **Central law** and a **State law** on a subject in the **Concurrent List**, the law made by the **Parliament** generally prevails. However, if the **State law** has received the **President's assent**, it can prevail in that specific state.
 
• **Residuary Powers (Article 248)**: The **Parliament** has the exclusive power to make any law with respect to any matter not enumerated in the **Concurrent List** or **State List**. These are known as **Residuary Powers**, and they belong to the **Union Government**.

questions.question: ‘Shad Pliang’, also known as the 'plate dance', is a traditional folk dance of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shad Pliang**, famously referred to as the **"Plate Dance"**, is a traditional folk dance belonging to the **North-Eastern** state of **Meghalaya**.
 
• This dance form is a unique cultural heritage of the **Khasi** community, who are one of the major indigenous tribes residing in the **Khasi Hills**.
 
• The performance is characterized by the incredible skill of the dancers—mostly **women**—who balance **brass plates** or metal dishes on their **fingertips** or palms while performing rhythmic movements.
 
• It is typically performed during **festivals**, **social gatherings**, and cultural programs to demonstrate the agility, balance, and grace of the local youth.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional musical instruments of **Meghalaya**, such as the **Tangmuri** (a wind instrument), **Nakra** (drum), and **Cymbals**, which provide a vibrant tempo to the performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Folk Dances of Meghalaya:**

 
 
• **Wangala Dance:** This is the most significant festival of the **Garo** tribe. Known as the **"100 Drums Festival"**, it is held in **November** to mark the end of the agricultural year and honor **Saljong**, the Sun God of fertility.
 
• **Nongkrem Dance:** A religious festival of the **Khasi** tribe performed at **Smit**. It is held annually to pray for a **bountiful harvest** and the prosperity of the people.
 
• **Shad Suk Mynsiem:** Known as the **"Dance of Peaceful Hearts"**, it is an annual spring dance celebrated in **April** by the **Khasi** people to express gratitude to the creator.
 
• **Laho Dance:** This dance belongs to the **Jaintia (Pnar)** tribe. It is performed by both **men and women** linked together, usually during the **Behdienkhlam** festival.
 
 
 
• **Dances of Other States mentioned in Options:**

• **Punjab:** Famous for high-energy dances such as **Bhangra** (performed by men), **Giddha** (performed by women), **Jhumar**, and **Malwai Giddha**.
 
• **Maharashtra:** Renowned for **Lavani**, **Koli** (the dance of the fisherfolk), **Dhangari Gaja**, and **Povadas** (ballads describing the life of **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj**).
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context:** **Meghalaya**, often called the **"Abode of Clouds"**, was carved out of **Assam** in **1972**. Its capital is **Shillong**, and it is globally famous for **Mawsynram** and **Cherrapunji**, which receive the **highest rainfall** in the world.

questions.question: The reference date for the census 2027 for the Union Territory of Ladakh shall be _________.

__

• In the context of the Indian Census, the **reference date** is the specific moment in time to which the census data refers, ensuring that the population count is a "snapshot" of the country at that exact instance.
 
• For most parts of India, the census reference date is typically the **1st of March** of the census year. However, for **snow-bound areas** and high-altitude regions like **Ladakh**, the date is set earlier to facilitate enumeration before the onset of extreme winter conditions which make transportation and communication impossible.
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs**, through the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, manages the scheduling and notification of these dates under the provisions of the **Census Act, 1948**.
 
• The choice of **October 1st** ensures that the administrative machinery can complete the head-counting process in the **Leh** and **Kargil** districts before heavy snowfall blocks the passes. ***Hence, the correct answer is 1st day of October 2026.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union Territory of Ladakh:**

 
 
• **Ladakh** was established as a **Union Territory** without a legislature on **October 31, 2019**, following the enactment of the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
 
• It is the **largest Union Territory** in India by area but has a very low population density due to its rugged mountainous terrain.
 
 
 
• **History of Census in India:**
 
 
• The first non-synchronous census in India was conducted in **1872** under **Lord Mayo**, while the first synchronous census took place in **1881**.
 
• Censuses are conducted every **10 years**. The **2021 Census** was significantly delayed due to the **COVID-19 pandemic**, leading to adjusted timelines for the subsequent data collection exercises.
 
 
 
• **Phases of Census:**

questions.question: In which Indian state is the festival of ‘Baithki Holi’ traditionally celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Baithki Holi** is a unique and culturally rich musical tradition of celebrating Holi, primarily observed in the **Kumaon region** of the state of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• Unlike the common celebration of colors, this tradition focuses on musical sittings (**Baithaks**) that commence as early as **Basant Panchami** and continue until the day of **Holi**.
 
• The songs performed during **Baithki Holi** are rooted in **Hindustani classical music**, where participants sing compositions based on specific **Raagas**.
 
• The musical sessions usually take place in the courtyards of homes or community centers, where people gather to celebrate the **spring season** through melody and rhythm.
 
• This form of celebration is a testament to the preservation of classical arts within the folk culture of the **Himalayan** foothills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Variations of Holi in Kumaon**:

 
 
• **Khari Holi**: This is the "standing" version of Holi where people in rural **Uttarakhand** wear traditional **white kurtas** and **churidar pyjamas**, dancing in circles to the beats of **Dhol** and **Hurka**.
 
• **Mahila Holi**: These are exclusive gatherings for **women**, where they sing songs related to social life, family, and devotion, marking a significant social outlet for the women of the hills.
 
 
 
• **Musical Elements**: The instruments predominantly used in these celebrations include the **Harmonium**, **Tabla**, and sometimes the **Dholak** or **Manjira**.
 
• **Regional Locations**: The tradition is most vibrant in districts such as **Almora**, **Nainital**, **Pithoragarh**, and **Champawat**. **Almora** is often considered the cultural hub for **Baithki Holi**.
 
• **Traditional Cuisine**: During these gatherings, traditional Kumaoni delicacies like **Aloo ke Gutke** (spicy potato dish), **Gujiya**, and **Singal** (a fried sweet snack) are served to the guests.
 
• **Language**: The lyrics of the songs are often a blend of **Braj Bhasha**, **Hindi**, and **Kumaoni**, often narrating the divine play of **Lord Krishna** and **Radha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Raagas**: In **Baithki Holi**, the **Raagas** sung change according to the time of the day. For instance, **Raag Bhairavi** might be sung in the morning, while **Raag Kafi** or **Khamaj** is preferred during the afternoon and evening.
 
• **Historical Context**: The tradition dates back several centuries and was historically patronized by the local **Chand dynasty** rulers and later preserved by the elite Brahmin and Kshatriya families of the **Kumaon** hills.
 
• **Symbolism**: The transition from the harsh **Himalayan winter** to the blossom of **spring** is the core theme, symbolizing renewal and communal harmony.
 
• **Holiyars**: The lead singers and participants of these musical sessions are locally referred to as **Holiyars**, who are respected for their knowledge of classical music and folk lore.

questions.question: The National Space Day of India is celebrated every year on August 23 to commemorate the _______.

options.text: successful soft-landing of the Vikram lander on the south pole of the moon
establishment of the Indian Space Research Organisation
successful launch of first satellite of India
successful launch of India's first interplanetary mission

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**successful soft-landing of the Vikram lander on the south pole of the moon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **August 23, 2023**, India scripted history as the **Chandrayaan-3** mission's **Vikram lander** successfully performed a **soft-landing** on the **lunar south pole**.
 
• To honor this landmark achievement in space exploration, Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** declared **August 23** as **National Space Day** during his address at **ISTRAC** in **Bengaluru**.
 
• With the success of this mission, **India** became the **fourth country** to achieve a soft landing on the **Moon** and the **very first country** to reach the **lunar south polar region**. ***Hence, option 1 is the correct statement.***
 
• The mission showcased India's advanced **technological capabilities** and **cost-effective** engineering, reinforcing its position as a global leader in the **space sector**.
 
• The **National Space Day** aims to inspire the **youth** of the country toward **Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM)** and celebrate India's journey in space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chandrayaan-3 Mission Details:**

 
 
• The mission was launched on **July 14, 2023**, from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota** using the **LVM3-M4** rocket.
 
• The mission components included a **Propulsion Module**, the **Vikram Lander** (named after **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**), and the **Pragyan Rover**.
 
• The **Pragyan Rover** successfully deployed and conducted chemical analysis of the **lunar surface** for one lunar day (approximately **14 Earth days**).
 
 
 
• **Significant Naming:**
 
 
• The landing site of **Chandrayaan-3** was named **Shiv Shakti Point**.
 
• The site where **Chandrayaan-2** left its footprints in **2019** was named **Tiranga Point**.
 
 
 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO):**
 
 
• **ISRO** was established on **August 15, 1969**, replacing the earlier **INCOSPAR**. ***Hence, statement 2 refers to the organization's founding, not National Space Day.***
 
• The first Indian satellite, **Aryabhata**, was launched on **April 19, 1975**. ***Hence, statement 3 refers to a different historic event.***
 
• India's first interplanetary mission, the **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)** or **Mangalyaan**, was launched on **November 5, 2013**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect in this context.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Theme of 2024:** The inaugural **National Space Day** celebrated in **2024** carried the theme **"Touching Lives while Touching the Moon: India's Space Saga"**.
 
• **Global Impact:** The landing near the **south pole** is scientifically significant because this region is believed to contain **water ice**, which could be vital for future **human settlements** and deep-space exploration.
 
• **Leadership:** The successful execution of **Chandrayaan-3** occurred under the leadership of **ISRO Chairman S. Somanath** and **Mission Director P. Veeramuthuvel**.
 
• **Financial Efficiency:** The total cost of the **Chandrayaan-3** mission was approximately **615 crore rupees**, which is significantly lower than many **Hollywood** space-themed movies, highlighting **India's** frugal but efficient **innovation**.

questions.question: Why should we wear cotton clothes in summer?

options.text: Cotton clothes prevent any evaporation of sweat.
Cotton clothes increase the body temperature by trapping heat.
Cotton clothes absorb sweat and help in its evaporation, which cools the body.
Cotton clothes are less absorbent and keep sweat on the skin.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cotton clothes absorb sweat and help in its evaporation, which cools the body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cotton** is a **natural fiber** that is highly **hydrophilic**, meaning it has a high capacity to **absorb water** or **moisture**.
 
• During **summer**, the human body produces more **sweat** as a biological mechanism to maintain **homeostasis** and regulate **internal temperature**.
 
• When we wear **cotton clothes**, the fabric **absorbs the sweat** from our skin and brings it into contact with the **atmosphere**.
 
• The **evaporation** of this sweat requires **energy**, which is taken from the **body surface** in the form of **heat**. This process is known as **evaporative cooling**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Cotton clothes prevent any evaporation of sweat**: This is incorrect because cotton actually facilitates evaporation by wicking moisture to the surface. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cotton clothes increase the body temperature by trapping heat**: Synthetic fibers like **wool** or certain **polyesters** trap heat, but cotton is **breathable** and allows heat to escape. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cotton clothes are less absorbent**: In reality, cotton can absorb up to **25 times** its weight in water, making it more absorbent than most **synthetic fabrics**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Latent Heat of Vaporization**: This is the **thermal energy** required to convert a liquid into a **gas** without changing its temperature. In the context of **summer cooling**, the sweat on the skin absorbs this **latent heat** from the body to evaporate, thereby **lowering the body temperature**.
 
• **Porosity of Cotton**: Cotton fibers are naturally **porous**. This **porosity** allows for better **air circulation** (breathability), which aids the **evaporation process** and prevents the growth of **bacteria** or **fungi** that thrive in stagnant, moist environments.
 
• **Comparison with Synthetic Fabrics**: Fabrics like **nylon** or **polyester** are **hydrophobic**. They do not absorb **sweat** effectively, causing it to remain trapped between the skin and the cloth, leading to **discomfort**, **skin rashes**, and a feeling of **suffocation** in **humid weather**.
 
• **Hypoallergenic Properties**: Cotton is a **hypoallergenic** material, making it ideal for **sensitive skin** during **summer** when **sweat-induced irritation** and **heat rashes** are common.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Color Matters**: In addition to the material, the **color** of the clothing is vital in **summer**. **Light-colored** cotton clothes reflect most of the **solar radiation** (heat) falling on them, whereas **dark colors** absorb it.
 
• **Molecular Structure**: The **cellulose** molecules in cotton contain **hydroxyl (-OH) groups** that attract **water molecules**, explaining its high **absorbency** compared to **petroleum-based** synthetic fibers.
 
• **Homeostasis**: The body's ability to keep its **internal environment** stable. **Sweating** is a primary method of **thermoregulation**, and choosing the right fabric like **cotton** assists the body in this **physiological** task.

• In the context of **India**, it is often referred to as the **agricultural sector** because **agriculture** is the most dominant activity within this category.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector**:

• **Tertiary Sector**:

• **Disguised Unemployment**: A major challenge in the **primary sector** is **disguised unemployment**, where more people are working than required, leading to low **marginal productivity**.

questions.question: Which State is the sole holder of the country's perlite resources?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gujarat** stands as the **sole holder** of the country's **perlite resources**. Perlite is a unique natural mineral that is found exclusively in this state within the borders of **India**.
 
• As per the **National Mineral Inventory** data maintained by the **Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM)**, the total resources of perlite in **India** as of **April 1, 2015**, are estimated at **2.41 million tonnes**.
 
• The entire quantity of these resources is concentrated in two specific districts of **Gujarat**: **Rajkot** and **Bhavnagar**. Significant occurrences have been reported in the **Osham Hill** area of **Rajkot** and near **Khadsaliya** in **Bhavnagar**.
 
• Of the total estimated resources, approximately **12%** (about **0.29 million tonnes**) fall under the **reserves** category, while the remaining **88%** (about **2.12 million tonnes**) are classified as **remaining resources**.
 
• Geologically, perlite in **Gujarat** is associated with the **acidic volcanic rocks** of the **Deccan Traps**, particularly those originating from the **Cretaceous to Eocene** periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition and Physical Properties:**

 
 
• **Perlite** is an amorphous volcanic glass that possesses a relatively high water content, typically between **2% to 5%**. It is formed by the hydration of **obsidian**.
 
• A distinctive feature of this mineral is its ability to **expand** significantly—up to **7 to 20 times** its original volume—when heated to temperatures ranging from **850°C to 1,100°C**. This process is known as "**popping**," similar to popcorn.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Horticulture:**
 
 
• Due to its **high porosity** and **low density**, expanded perlite is widely used as a **soil amendment** to improve aeration and drainage.
 
• It is a staple in **hydroponics** and greenhouse farming because it is **sterile**, has a **neutral pH**, and does not degrade over time.
 
 
 
• **Construction and Industrial Uses:**
 
 
• In the **construction industry**, it is utilized as a lightweight aggregate in **concrete and plaster**, offering superior **thermal insulation** and **fire-resistant** properties.
 
• It is also employed as a **filter aid** in the processing of liquids, including **beer**, **wine**, **sugar**, and **pharmaceuticals**, because of its ability to trap minute impurities without affecting the chemical composition of the fluid.
 
 
 
• **Global and Indian Context:**
 
 
• While **Gujarat** is the only Indian producer, on a global scale, countries like **Greece**, **Turkey**, and the **USA** are the leading producers of perlite.
 
• In **India**, the demand for perlite is growing in the **cryogenic insulation** sector, where it is used to insulate tanks holding **liquefied gases** at extremely low temperatures.

questions.question: After which of the following country joining, BRIC transformed into BRICS?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South Africa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The acronym **BRIC** was originally coined by **Jim O'Neill**, an economist at **Goldman Sachs**, in a **2001** paper titled "Building Better Global Economic BRICs."
 
• The original group consisted of four major emerging national economies: **Brazil**, **Russia**, **India**, and **China**.
 
• The **first formal summit** of the BRIC nations was held on **June 16, 2009**, in **Yekaterinburg**, **Russia**, focusing on improving the global economic situation and reforming financial institutions.
 
• **South Africa** was officially invited to join the group in **December 2010**, following a series of diplomatic efforts to include a representative from the **African continent**.
 
• With the inclusion of **South Africa**, the group's name was formally changed to **BRICS**. The "S" in the acronym stands for **South Africa**.
 
• **South Africa** attended its first summit as a full member during the **3rd BRICS Summit** held in **Sanya**, **China**, on **April 14, 2011**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives and Cooperation**:

 
 
• The primary objective of **BRICS** is to enhance **economic cooperation**, **political coordination**, and **cultural exchange** among its member states.
 
• The group aims to promote a **multipolar world order** and challenge the dominance of Western-led global financial systems such as the **World Bank** and the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**.
 
 
 
• **New Development Bank (NDB)**:
 
 
• During the **6th BRICS Summit** in **Fortaleza**, **Brazil** (**2014**), the member nations signed an agreement to establish the **New Development Bank**, headquartered in **Shanghai**, **China**.
 
• The **NDB** was created to mobilize resources for **infrastructure** and **sustainable development projects** in BRICS and other emerging economies.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance**:
 
 
• Collectively, the **BRICS** nations represent about **41%** of the **global population**, nearly **24%** of the **world's GDP**, and approximately **16%** of **global trade**.
 
• The group serves as a significant platform for **South-South cooperation**.
 
 
 
• **Expansion (BRICS+)**:
 
 
• In **August 2023**, during the **15th BRICS Summit** in **Johannesburg**, **South Africa**, the group announced a historic expansion.
 
• New members invited to join included **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran**, **Saudi Arabia**, and the **United Arab Emirates**, with their membership becoming effective on **January 1, 2024**.

questions.question: In which year did the GDP of India crossed the 1 trillion-dollar mark?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2007**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** officially crossed the **$1 trillion** mark in the year **2007**.
 
• With this achievement, India became the **12th nation** in the world to join the "trillion-dollar club."
 
• The milestone was reached during the tenure of **Dr. Manmohan Singh** as the **Prime Minister** and **P. Chidambaram** as the **Union Finance Minister**.
 
• This significant economic expansion was fueled by a period of robust growth where the Indian economy grew at an average rate of approximately **8-9%** between **2003** and **2007**.
 
• The primary drivers for reaching this milestone included the booming **Service Sector**, increased **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, and strong domestic consumption.
 
• It took India nearly **60 years** after its **Independence** in **1947** to reach the first trillion dollars in terms of **Nominal GDP**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Growth Trajectory:**

 
 
• After crossing **$1 trillion** in **2007**, it took India only **seven years** to reach the **$2 trillion** mark in **2014**.
 
• The **$3 trillion** milestone was achieved in **2019**, showing an accelerated pace of economic accumulation despite global headwinds.
 
 
 
• **Economic Rankings:**
 
 
• As of **2023-24**, India is the **5th largest economy** in the world by **Nominal GDP**, trailing behind the **USA**, **China**, **Germany**, and **Japan**.
 
• In terms of **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**, India is ranked as the **3rd largest economy** globally.
 
 
 
• **GDP Definition:**
 
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** represents the total monetary or market value of all the finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period, usually a **financial year**.
 
• The **Real GDP** is adjusted for inflation, while **Nominal GDP** uses current market prices without inflation adjustment.
 
 
 
• **Future Targets:**
 
 
• The **Government of India** has set an ambitious target to make India a **$5 trillion economy**. This goal involves heavy investments in **infrastructure**, **digital transformation**, and the **manufacturing sector** through initiatives like **Make in India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 1991 Reforms:** The foundation for reaching the trillion-dollar mark was laid by the **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms introduced in **1991** by the then Finance Minister **Manmohan Singh** under Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao**.
 
• **Sectoral Contribution:** By **2007**, the **Services Sector** contributed more than **50%** to India's GDP, signifying a shift from an agrarian-based economy to a service-led growth model.
 
• **Global Context:** The **2007** milestone was particularly notable as it preceded the **2008 Global Financial Crisis**; India's strong internal demand helped it remain relatively resilient during the subsequent global downturn.
 
• **Statistical Agencies:** In India, GDP is calculated by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.

questions.question: Which of the following sports event NOT use a stick?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shot Put**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shot Put** is a track and field event where the athlete "puts" (pushes) a heavy **spherical metal ball** (the shot) as far as possible. It is a pure test of explosive strength and does not utilize any form of a stick or pole for the throw. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***
 
• **Hockey** is a popular team sport (both **Field Hockey** and **Ice Hockey**) where players must use a **hockey stick** to maneuver, pass, and hit a ball or puck into the opponent's goal. The stick is the primary tool used by the players. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Javelin Throw** is an athletics event where the equipment used is a **spear-like stick** known as a javelin. It is approximately **2.5 meters** in length and is thrown after a run-up. The javelin itself is effectively a long, tapered **stick** made of **metal** or **carbon fiber**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Pole Vault** is a field event in **Athletics** where an individual uses a long, flexible **pole** (which is technically a long stick) to jump over a high crossbar. The **pole** is an essential piece of equipment without which the sport cannot be performed. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Shot Put.***

• The event takes place within a **throwing circle** with a **diameter of 2.135 meters** (7 feet).
 
• Two main techniques are used: the **Glide** (pioneered by **Parry O'Brien**) and the **Rotational** (spin) technique.
 
 
 
• **Javelin Throw Details:**
 
 
• The **Javelin** must be held at the grip and thrown over-the-shoulder. For **men**, the javelin weighs **800 grams**, and for **women**, it weighs **600 grams**.
 
• Famous athletes in this field include **Neeraj Chopra** from **India**, who won the **Gold Medal** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Pole Vault Details:**
 
 
• The **poles** used today are made from high-tech materials like **fiberglass** or **carbon fiber** to provide maximum flexibility and energy return.
 
• The current world record holder is **Armand Duplantis**, who has pushed the limits of the sport by clearing heights over **6.20 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Hockey Stick Evolution:**
 
 
• Historically, **hockey sticks** were made from **mulberry** or **ash wood**. Modern sticks are now made from **composite materials** including **fiberglass**, **kevlar**, and **carbon fiber** for better durability and power.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• The **Shot Put** ball must have a smooth surface and be perfectly spherical. Any indentation or "grip" on the ball is prohibited.
 
• While **Javelin**, **Hockey**, and **Pole Vault** rely on the physics of the "stick" (leveraging length and flexibility), **Shot Put** relies entirely on the **kinetic chain** of the athlete's body to propel the mass of the ball.

questions.question: Around which fort did the city of Chennai develop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fort Saint George**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fort Saint George** is historically recognized as the first **English fortress** in **India**, founded in **1644** in the coastal city of **Madras**, which is now known as **Chennai**.
 
• The construction of the fort was initiated by the **British East India Company** through its agents, **Francis Day** and **Andrew Cogan**, who secured the grant of land from the local **Nayaka** rulers in **1639**.
 
• The city of **Chennai** effectively developed and expanded around this fort, which served as a nucleus for **British** administrative and commercial activities in **South India** for centuries.
 
• Historically, the settlement within the fort walls was referred to as **White Town**, while the indigenous settlements that grew outside the walls were known as **Black Town** (later renamed **George Town**).
 
• Today, the fort continues to be a vital administrative hub, housing the **Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly** and the **Secretariat** of the **Government of Tamil Nadu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Named after **King William III**, the current structure was completed in **1781** following the **British** victory in the **Battle of Plassey** to prevent future attacks from **Bengal Nawabs**.

questions.question: The advent of Purandaradasa, in the year ____, marked a very important landmark in the development of Carnatic music.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1484**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The advent of **Purandaradasa** in the year **1484** marked a monumental shift in the evolution of **Carnatic music**, leading him to be revered as the **"Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha"** (the Grandfather of Carnatic Music).
 
• Born as **Srinivasa Nayaka** in **Purandharagad** (near **Shimoga**, **Karnataka**), he was a wealthy diamond merchant before renouncing his worldly possessions to become a wandering devotee of **Lord Vitthala**.
 
• He is credited with **systematizing the teaching methodology** of Carnatic music by introducing a graded syllabus that is still followed by students today, centuries later.
 
• **Purandaradasa** introduced the raga **Mayamalavagowla** as the basic scale for music instruction. This choice was revolutionary because the scale’s symmetrical structure helps beginners grasp the nuances of **swaras** (notes) more effectively than other ragas.
 
• He composed foundational exercises including **Svaravalis** (basic notes), **Janti Varisas** (double notes), **Alankaras** (rhythmic patterns), and **Geethams** (simple songs), which form the bedrock of **Carnatic vocal and instrumental training**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Haridasa Movement:**

 
 
• **Purandaradasa** was a prominent figure in the **Haridasa** movement of **Karnataka**, a devotional movement dedicated to **Lord Vishnu**.
 
• He was a disciple of the great philosopher-saint **Vyasaraya**, who famously remarked that "Among the devotees, Purandara Dasa is the greatest."
 
• The movement utilized **music and poetry** in the local **Kannada** language to spread **Bhakti** (devotion) and social reform among the common people.
 
 
 
• **Composition and Style:**
 
 
• His compositions are known as **Devaranamas** or **Dasapadas**. Legend suggests he composed **475,000** songs, though only about **1,000** are currently available.
 
• He used the pen name (**Ankita Nama**) **'Purandara Vitthala'** at the end of each composition to signify his devotion.
 
• His lyrics often dealt with **social issues**, criticizing caste discrimination, hypocrisy, and greed, while emphasizing the importance of an **inner spiritual life**.
 
 
 
• **Influence on Later Musicians:**
 
 
• The technical structure he established paved the way for the **"Trinity of Carnatic Music"** (**Tyagaraja**, **Muthuswami Dikshitar**, and **Syama Sastri**) who lived in the **18th century**.
 
• **Saint Tyagaraja** openly acknowledged the influence of **Purandaradasa** in his own musical development and spiritual journey.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** **Purandaradasa** lived during the peak of the **Vijayanagara Empire**, particularly during the reign of **Krishnadevaraya**. This era was a **Golden Age** for art, culture, and literature in **South India**.
 
• **Dates and Timeline:** While he was born in **1484**, he passed away in **1564**, just a year before the fall of the **Vijayanagara Empire** in the **Battle of Talikota** (**1565**).
 
• **Cultural Impact:** His contribution transformed music from a complex courtly art into a medium of **mass spiritual expression**. By simplifying the language to **Kannada** and focusing on **rhythm and melody**, he made classical music accessible to all layers of society.
 
• **Pedagogy:** Even today, every student of **Carnatic music** begins their journey by practicing the **Sarali Varisas** in **Raga Mayamalavagowla**, exactly as prescribed by **Purandaradasa** over **500 years ago**.
